name: Semi-dwarf wheat breeding, Mexico
summary: Short, stiff-strawed, high-yielding wheats bred in Mexico by Norman Borlaug's programme from Norin 10 dwarfing genes, released by 1962 and later grown across South Asia.
description: In 1953 Norman Borlaug's programme in Mexico began crossing Orville Vogel's semi-dwarf wheats, which carried dwarfing genes from the Japanese variety Norin 10, with Mexican varieties. After a failed first attempt and repeated crossing, the result was short, stiff-strawed spring wheats that resisted lodging; two of them, Pitic 62 and Penjamo 62, were released for commercial production by 1962. Later varieties such as Sonora 64 and Lerma Rojo 64 led to the Green Revolution in India, Pakistan and other countries.

impact.note: The Mexican semi-dwarfs doubled Mexican yields and were taken up in India, Pakistan, Turkey and other countries (reach 2, not 3: the source measures hectares and seed shipments, not most of humanity, so the lower score is taken), let wheat turn heavy fertiliser into grain without lodging (depth 2), and began a long line of high-yielding varieties and the Green Revolution pattern (generativity 2).

why: After unsuccessfully screening the USDA world wheat collection for shorter, strong varieties, Borlaug wrote to Vogel for seed with the Norin 10 dwarfing genes.

date.basis: As the cited source gives it.

events.statement: In 1953 Borlaug began crossing Vogel's semi-dwarf winter wheat varieties with Mexican varieties.

evidence.supports: In 1953, Borlaug began crossing Vogel’s semi-dwarf winter wheat varieties with Mexican varieties.

date.label: by 1962
date.basis: As the cited source gives it.

events.statement: By 1962 two high-yielding semi-dwarf Norin 10 derivatives, Pitic 62 and Penjamo 62, had been released for commercial production in Mexico.

evidence.supports: By 1962, 10 years after Vogel first supplied seed of the Norin 10 semi-dwarf progeny to Borlaug, two high-yielding semi-dwarf Norin 10 derivatives, Pitic 62 and Penjamo 62 , were released for commercial production.

earliest_record.rationale: The earliest dated evidence found for this capability in this community. No review has yet confirmed that nothing earlier exists.

unresolved.note: Norin 10 (the 1935 Japanese cross, credited to Gonjoro Inazuka by CIMMYT) and Vogel's semi-dwarf winter wheats at Washington State (late 1940s; Gaines) are separate achievements that need their own records, to which this one should then be linked.

The release years of Pitic 62 and Penjamo 62 are given as 1962 in the table of the National Academy memoir; the breeding stations (Sonora and central Mexico in the lead) are not named on the cited page, so the place is Mexico only.
IR8 rice (1966) and the Japanese and Italian semi-dwarf wheats need their own records if the curator agrees.

research.note: CIMMYT's account says S. D. Salmon took Norin 10 samples from Japan to the United States, Orville Vogel at Washington State University bred semi-dwarf wheats from it, and Borlaug asked Vogel for seed with the Norin 10 dwarfing genes; the National Academy memoir of Borlaug likewise says he obtained the Rht1 and Rht2 genes from Vogel.
